transcript: We talk a lot about how scary the future of Broadway can feel, but after meeting the next generation of theater artists, I actually left with a lot of hope. I got to spend the day with springboard to design, an incredible tuition free summer program that brings under represented students to New York City and introduces them to the world of theatrical design. Through mentorships and workshops and backstage experiences, these students get unprecedented access to see how Broadway gets made. I got to join them for a tour four of a Broadway costume shop with Tony winning designer Clint Ramos. And let me be real, I was geeking out as much as they were. We got a super up close look at these stunning craftsmanship of Broadway costumes. We Learned every step from design to the stage and Learned how costumes are built, fitted, altered, and maintained. Could not get over how detailed and intricate everything was. The amount of hand sewing gems and sequin and making ruffles and tassels. And it was so much fun watching these students ask incredibly thoughtful and interesting questions. It's a reminder that every show you love is built by hundreds of artists, and springboard to design is giving them a chance to realize that they could be one for themselves. I've made a little costume change and now I'm gonna go meet the students and catch the Jellicle Ball. I'm so excited to see them watch the show. And it's the show Again, I love this musical so much, and I feel like it's gonna be really special to watch with a group of young, excited theater people who've never been. I actually can't imagine a better musical to take design students to than cats the Jellicle Ball. And that was before we even knew that Lin Manuel Miranda was going to be our guest judge. Watching this show alongside students who noticed every costume, every wig, every lighting choice is something I will truly never forget. I love getting to watch everyone's joyful reactions and hear their insights during the intermission. Programs like springboard to design are so important for this reason. Many of these students have never had the chance to come to New York or see Broadway before, and now they can see where a place for them might exist in this industry. If. If you're a student who loves theatre, fashion, sewing, painting, design, make sure to check out springboard to Design's next cohort. I had the best time with them, and I cannot wait to see what they create next.
